Anthropic CEO Amodei admits "there's a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year" days before a record IPO
items.excerpt: Days before what could be the largest IPO in history, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying compute 'the deepest business dilemma' his company faces. Anthropic's commitments now total nearly $901 billion, and it's still far from clear whether future revenue will justify those costs. The planned IPO is largely meant to serve as a financial buffer against that uncertainty. items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
items.excerpt: For the first time in a while, no OpenAI model leads the MathArena AI math benchmark. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Anthropic's Fable 5.2 have knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top, though both cost significantly more. Gemini ignored the time limit in testing and almost never gave up on a task. The article Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
items.excerpt: OpenAI is dissolving its standalone robotics team for the second time, but not because it lacks data. General-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can apparently control robots directly, making a dedicated unit unnecessary. The researchers are being redistributed across other teams in what the company frames as a way to accelerate its robotics efforts. The article OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Anthropic can already retrain Mythos with "a fraction of the compute originally needed," says former researcher Coxon
items.excerpt: Former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon points to a slide from Anthropic's IPO roadshow as a reason he left, saying it shows the company's algorithms are improving not just quickly but at an accelerating rate. Coxon continues to call for a pause on frontier model development so competitors can catch up and human-level AI can become a commodity. items.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
items.excerpt: Runway releases its robotics model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses knowledge from video training for robot control and leads the World Action Model category on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 benchmark. It can't yet plan complex action sequences on its own, though. The article Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5
items.excerpt: Anthropic has made Claude Opus 5.5 the default model on all paid plans and published a guide that does away with old prompting habits. The main takeaway is to drop "think hard" and start at Medium effort. The article Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5 appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy
items.excerpt: Cmpnd released dspy-wsp, a prototype DSPy optimizer for weight-space programming. A frontier LLM reads a small model’s weights, edits them in a sandbox, and tests each change, with no gradients and about $5 to $10 per run. The post Cmpnd Releases dspy-wsp: Weight-Space Programming Comes to DSPy appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Vercel Releases UI SDK: 50+ UI Behaviors for AI Coding Agents
items.excerpt: Vercel Labs released Vercel UI SDK, an Apache-2.0 beta library of 50+ UI behaviors. Coding agents compose them into accessible components for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, with a bridge for direct UI control. The post Vercel Releases UI SDK: 50+ UI Behaviors for AI Coding Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Stanford Research Open-Sources Memorilla, a Latent Memory Module for Frozen LLMs
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers released Memorilla, an open-source memory system that compresses a document collection into 16 memory tokens for a frozen Qwen3-8B. It reaches 84.33% on FactKG using 108x fewer document tokens than full context. The post Stanford Research Open-Sources Memorilla, a Latent Memory Module for Frozen LLMs appeared first on MarkTechPost .
